Emma — thanks, and glad the demo landed. Quick reply with a high-level option set (we can pick one for the amendment):

Option A — Fixed-burst credit pool (recommended for predictable billing)
- Customer has a monthly reserved commit (e.g., 48 GPU-hours/day) + a burst credit pool equal to X% of monthly commit.
- Bursts consume credits first; credits replenish monthly. Overages beyond credits billed at pre-agreed overage rate.
- Preemption: when reserved+credits exhausted, requests fallback to preemptible slab (lower cost, up to 2x latency).

Option B — Time-windowed burst lanes (recommended for traffic spikes)
- Allocate short-duration burst lanes (e.g., 2–6 hour windows) that do not consume monthly commit but are billed separately on a per-window basis.
- SLO shedding: during lane exhaustion, critical routes stay on reserved capacity; noncritical background jobs are throttled or queued.

Option C — Hybrid credit + graceful SLO degrade (recommended for ML training + inference mix)
- Credits for inference bursts; preemptible routing for training bursts.
- If latency SLO jeopardized, automatic model fallback to a smaller quantized variant and partial token trimming to preserve 95th-pct latency while allowing reduced-quality outputs.

I'll pull together a one-page amendment snippet with exact formulas and an ops runbook excerpt for fallback. Attaching a draft capacity mapping (WIP) and a matrix of SLO-shedding behaviors.

—Mateo
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity-mapping-novaflux.xlsx (xlsx)]

Quick internal: Procurement will want a conservative threshold for automatic alerts and one human escalation path. My suggested defaults:
- Alerting: when burst credit usage > 60% of pool in a 2h window OR projected exhaustion within 24h.
- Escalation: automated email to NovaFlux SRE + Redwood CS, page Redwood on-call if exhaustion within 6h.
- Pricing: tiered overage bands (0–10% at 1.5x, 10–30% at 2x, >30% negotiated).

Also proposing we include a clause for a 48h advance notice for scheduled large-scale training (pre-emptible lane reservation) to avoid noisy transient spikes that hammer preemptible capacity.

—Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Dedicated burst lane crediting — amendment snippet and mitigation order (draft)

Emma/Liam/procurement — attached is a short draft amendment snippet and the SLO mitigation order we discussed. Key points in plain language:

Amendment (draft summary) — Burst Credits Model
- Formula: For every $1,000 of monthly committed reserved spend, NovaFlux receives 24 GPU-hours of burst credit (billed at the committed rate). Credits apply to inference traffic only; training-run bursts are billed as overage unless previously reserved.
- Replenishment: Credits reset at the start of each billing month. Unused credits do not roll over.
- Overage: After credits are exhausted, overage is billed at 2.0x the committed GPU-hour rate unless NovaFlux purchases additional on-demand windows or uses preemptible slab routing.

SLO Mitigation Order (automated stack — deterministic order)
1) Prefix/KV cache warming and local routing prioritization (preserve user-facing short calls).
2) Route less-latency-sensitive jobs (batch scoring, retraining) to preemptible slab.
3) Automatic model fallback to the quantized 8-bit variant for heavy endpoints (single-step degrade).
4) Rate-limit noncritical routes with exponential backoff and queueing (configurable per-route).
5) If the 99th-pct latency is still not within target, temporarily divert to a smaller model family and notify NovaFlux SRE + Redwood CS for manual remediation.

Operational guarantees / alerts
- Thresholds: we recommend alerting at 50% credit use in 1h and critical paging at projected exhaustion within 8h.
- Runbook: Redwood will provide a 2-page runbook for the on-call and a 24h contact for urgent capacity negotiations.

Attachments: draft amendment (PDF), capacity mapping XLSX, SLO-shedding matrix (PNG).

Next steps
- Agree on the credit formula (proposal above) or send an alternate per-GPU-hour number and we will calculate credits.
- If procurement approves the snippet, I'll loop Legal for a short amendment.

Action items assigned:
- NovaFlux: indicate whether you prefer the $1,000 -> 24 GPU-hours mapping or a direct GPU-hour price. (Liam)
- Redwood: Legal to prepare amendment after confirmation (Mateo).
- Redwood Ops: produce the 2-page runbook and alert thresholds (Jasmine/Marcus).

—Mateo
